name: HHV-8-associated Multicentric Castleman Disease

ethnicAssociations: More common in individuals of African descent

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Consensus Diagnostic Criteria for HHV-8-associated Multicentric Castleman Disease

criteria.description: Characteristic lymph node histopathology showing plasmablastic or hyaline vascular features with HHV-8 positivity
Multicentric lymphadenopathy with systemic inflammatory symptoms such as fever, night sweats, and weight loss
Elevated inflammatory markers (e.g., CRP, ESR), anemia, thrombocytopenia, and elevated IL-6 levels
Detection of HHV-8 DNA or latent nuclear antigen in affected tissues or blood
Exclusion of other lymphoproliferative disorders and infections

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic lymph node histopathology with HHV-8 positivity plus multicentric lymphadenopathy and systemic symptoms
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, histopathological, and virological data.

pathognomonic.notes: Enlargement of multiple lymph node groups

pathognomonic.symptomName: HHV-8 viral antigen positivity in lymphoid tissue
pathognomonic.notes: Detection of HHV-8 latent nuclear antigen by immunohistochemistry
searchTerms: HHV-8 virus detected in lymph tissue
presence of HHV-8 viral proteins in lymph nodes

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic histological pattern in affected nodes
searchTerms: lymph node with immature plasma cells
aggressive plasma cell tumor in lymph node
plasmablastic cell changes in lymph node biopsy
immune system destroying red blood cells
red blood cell breakdown from antibodies

laboratory: Elevated C-reactive protein (CRP) and erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR)
Anemia and thrombocytopenia on complete blood count
Detection of HHV-8 DNA by PCR in blood or tissue
imaging: CT or PET-CT showing multicentric lymphadenopathy
Hepatosplenomegaly on abdominal ultrasound or CT
genetic: Presence of HHV-8 viral genome in affected tissues
other: Lymph node biopsy demonstrating plasmablastic or hyaline vascular histology with HHV-8 latent nuclear antigen positivity

distinguishingFeatures: Monocentric lymphadenopathy versus multicentric in MCD
Presence of malignant lymphoma cells on biopsy
Lack of characteristic HHV-8 plasmablastic histology

redFlags: Rapidly progressive lymphadenopathy with systemic inflammatory symptoms
Severe cytopenias (anemia, thrombocytopenia) indicating marrow involvement
Signs of organ dysfunction such as renal impairment or pulmonary infiltrates
references: Fajgenbaum DC, Uldrick TS, Bagg A, et al. International, evidence-based consensus diagnostic criteria for HHV-8–associated multicentric Castleman disease. Blood. 2020;135(20):1819-1829.

Polizzotto MN, Uldrick TS, Hu D, et al. Clinical Manifestations of Kaposi Sarcoma Herpesvirus Lytic Activation: Multicentric Castleman Disease (KSHV-MCD) and the KSHV Inflammatory Cytokine Syndrome. Front Microbiol. 2012;3:73.
Dispenzieri A, Fajgenbaum DC. Overview of Castleman disease. Blood. 2020;135(16):1353-1364.
